readings.evidence: In the native tile the line runs from about x 2374-2914, y 3856-3956. It stands alone, with no shelfmark or title on its own ruled line. The L-shaped mark is at about x 3054-3159, y 3846-3886. The fol. 182 image shows '…706' at its left edge; this is the same target-page line seen across the gutter, not a separate note. The parent holding cannot be determined from the page.

The prefix letter is a C/c-like curve with a horizontal stroke through it. It looks like E written over c, or the reverse, and the order of the writing is not determinable. The middle digit of 383 has a looped, 8-like shape (the overview looks like '303'). The last digit of the RLM number has an open, loose top and is more like 8 than 3. There are possible small dots near the L and after the M of RLM; whether these are stops is not clear.

On fol. 182 the matching '→' is at about native y 4136-4176. The d.555(6) shelfmark row is at about y 4100-4130 and the c.324(6) row at about y 3866. The arrow therefore sits just below the d.555(6) row, which suggests an insertion after the Manīṣāpañcaka group. No text states the position.

On fol. 182 the L mark and the short stroke are at about native y 3816-3856. This is level with the √c.324(6) Manīṣāpañcaka row, at about y 3866. The extent 'ff. 1-6' also occurs in b002, but there is no physical link between the two lines.
The mark after 5475 has a short downward tail, more comma-like than a plain stop, but it is ambiguous. The other two readings are treated separately in issues 07 and 08.
The superscript is a b-like letter with a small mark beneath it. This is consistent with the supplied label.
The final letter is a looped e-form, matching the e-forms elsewhere in the same hand. The reading has not been changed.
The first letter is a single slightly curved vertical stroke with no serifs. It is ambiguous between I and l.
The macrons and underdots are small and cursive. The underdots under ṣ and ṇ appear present, but not every diacritic is verifiable.
The V is separated from the 'd' and matches the tick marks before shelfmarks on the adjacent pages.
